candidates.comment: Hi, thanks for getting back to me. Once you have gone past the 4Vdc supply level (you were previously using a 3.7V battery), you are within the recommended power supply voltage levels, so you won’t really get much more out of this little amp. Assuming that you have a 10uF capacitor between pins 1 & 8 on the chip, (this gives a gain of 200) then you are also at max gain. As mentioned before, the LM386 audio chip used in this kit is the lower O/P version LM386-N1. If you swap for a LM386-N4 it will give you a little more gain and hence, a slightly higher output. However, please bear in mind though that this little amp is used primarily for small portable devices like radios etc. If you need a lot more power then you may need to look at a different amplifier. BTW not sure if you have one or two speakers connected, but their impedance should be between 4 & 16 ohms. Might be worth checking, as if you have two 4ohm speakers connected in parallel, it would result in a 2ohm load for the amp which may cause issues. Hope this helps – please come back to me if I can assist you any further

candidates.comment:
Hi, that sounds a very interesting project. Your speaker connections to SP+ - are correct. If you not getting any O/P, you might want to re-check a few items:

1. Check the polarity of your DC supply connections if you are using the 3.5mm jack as it is easy to get these crossed.
2. Check that all the electrolytic capacitors are correctly connected polarity wise.
3. Check for any unintended solder bridges.
4. Check that the DIL socket is not fitted the opposite way round & hence, the LM38 chip may end up being fitted 180 deg. to what it should be.
5. Check for any dry solder joints
6. If still no joy, try another speaker.

I would be interested on how you get on. Thanks for getting touch.
TWCG

candidates.comment: Hi, sorry to hear your little amp didn't work out. However, it would be worth checking a few things before you give up. These might sound a little basic, but I have done some of these myself on more than a few occasions! Firstly, ensure that electrolytic capacitors have been correctly fitted as they are polarised & so will not perform reversed. Is the LM386 fitted the correct way around, (and a check to see if a pin has been bent)? Suggest you also check for any dry joints, (sometimes component leads require a quick rub with fine wet and dry to remove oxidisation especially if new old stock items are used), solder bridges between PCB tracks etc.  All worth checking - good luck!
